record.context_brief: Maximum number of MUBs outside prime-power dimensions
record.original_question: For complex Hilbert-space dimensions N that are not prime powers, determine how many mutually unbiased bases can exist. Here a set of bases in H_N is mutually unbiased when each basis is orthonormal and, for any two different bases, every squared overlap between one vector from each basis equals 1/N; no more than N+1 such bases can exist, prime-power dimensions achieve N+1, and the non-prime-power case remains unresolved.

evidence.quote: These bases are called mutually unbiased if any two bases are unbiased, which means ∀i,j ∣⟨ψm i ∣ψn j ⟩∣2= 1 N , m ≠ n. (2) It is relatively easy to show that there exist no more than N + 1 MUBs in HN.
If N is a power of a prime, various properties of a complete set ofN+1 MUBs are already understood [43–47], but otherwise the number of existing MUBs remains unknown [48–50].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $N\geq 2$ be a positive integer and let $\mathcal{H}_N=\mathbb{C}^N$ with its standard Hermitian inner product. A collection of orthonormal bases $\{|\psi^{(1)}_i\rangle\}_{i=1}^N,\dots,\{|\psi^{(M)}_i\rangle\}_{i=1}^N$ of $\mathcal{H}_N$ is called a set of mutually unbiased bases (MUBs) if, for every pair of distinct bases $m\neq n$ and all indices $i,j\in\{1,\dots,N\}$,
$$|\langle \psi^{(m)}_i\,|\,\psi^{(n)}_j\rangle|^2=\frac{1}{N}.$$
It is known that any set of MUBs in $\mathcal{H}_N$ has cardinality at most $N+1$, and that this bound is attained whenever $N$ is a prime power.

Determine, for every dimension $N$ that is not a prime power, the maximum cardinality $M(N)$ of a set of mutually unbiased bases in $\mathbb{C}^N$. In particular, decide whether $M(6)=3$ or whether four mutually unbiased bases can exist in $\mathbb{C}^6$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem remains open. Dimension 6 is the smallest non-prime-power case and it is still unknown whether more than 3 mutually unbiased bases exist in C^6 (the conjectured maximum is 3, and no set of 4 MUBs has ever been found, despite extensive analytical and numerical searches). Recent work in 2025 reformulates the question as a polynomial optimization problem and shows the algorithm would in principle resolve dimension 6 but remains computationally intractable. A 2025 note also invalidated some structural theorems previously claimed about hypothetical sets of 4 MUBs in C^6.

status_evidence.title: Mutually unbiased bases - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Dimension 6 is the smallest dimension for which the number of mutually unbiased bases is not known; the conjecture is that the maximal number is 3.
status_evidence.claim: The maximum number of MUBs in C^6 is unknown; conjectured to be 3.

status_evidence.title: Mutually unbiased bases as a commuting polynomial optimization problem
status_evidence.snippet: An algorithm that would eventually solve the open question in dimension six with finite memory, although it still remains computationally intractable.
status_evidence.claim: Recent 2025 work confirms the dimension-6 question is still open.

status_evidence.title: Reply to Comment on 'Product states and Schmidt rank of MUBs in dimension six'
status_evidence.snippet: April 2025 work continues to investigate structural properties of hypothetical sets of 4 MUBs in C^6.
status_evidence.claim: Active research in 2025 still treats the existence of 4 MUBs in C^6 as an open question.
